In this Head of Employee Experience role, you'll be…

• 
Setting the vision and one roadmap for our Employee Experience across the employee journey, so colleagues experience one Formalize in every office and every new country.

• 
Building a scalable, intuitive model where people, systems, processes, IT and offices simply work, so day-to-day operations run smoothly on their own, freeing up your team to give personal, high-touch support when it matters most

• 
Setting up one front door for every question on people, workplace and IT, with one ticketing system and a shared knowledge base, solving most questions through self-serve and the rest first time.

• 
Leading a team of around ten across People Operations, Workplace and Internal IT with clear ownership, and making your team's time here a real springboard for their HR careers.

• 
Owning workplace standards, vendors and budgets, and opening new offices on time and on budget from one playbook.

• 
Working with our People Business Partners and Talent Acquisition on journeys that cross teams, such as onboarding and country launches.

Who is the Employee Experience team?

Employee Experience is the team that treats our colleagues like our best customers. We bring People Operations, Workplace, and Internal IT together under one roof because a great workday relies on all three: a contract and conversations that make sense, an office where we celebrate wins together, and a laptop that works from hour one.

Within People Operations, a back office sets standards, systems and automation, while People Operations Partners in the front office are the daily face for colleagues. Our People Business Partners, focused on managers and leaders, work closely with us.

Our principle is high touch where it matters, effortless everywhere else, with one front door for every question and the ambition that colleagues hardly need us.

What you bring

• 
Proven leadership experience across the broader employee experience spectrum, combining People Operations with workplace and internal IT, ideally in a scaling international tech company.

• 
A builder's instinct. Your energy comes from systems, standards and support models that work every day. Events and celebrations matter but aren't the core, so if confetti is what drives you, this probably isn't your role.

• 
You think in models, linking the structural basis to the human interaction it enables, and you know where high personal-touch adds value and where good design does the job better.

• 
Strong on digital: people systems, automation and AI are how the team scales, and you're comfortable owning tooling decisions and the budget behind them.

• 
A strong sense of fairness and consistency, with standards explicit enough to guide people rather than slow them down.

• 
A hands-on leader who builds teams across disciplines and grows people into bigger roles.

• 
Clear communication in English, the credibility to partner effectively with our leadership team, and the ability to work from our Copenhagen office (or Aarhus).

What do we offer you?

• 
A monthly salary ranging from 65,000 to 70,000 DKK.

• 
Continuous development through a clear and transparent career framework, so you always know what the next step looks like, with biannual growth talks and regular check-ins.

• 
Thorough pre- and onboarding to set you up for success.

• 
A culture of ownership, trust and independence, with the support you need.

• 
An office-first culture in a central location in Copenhagen or Aarhus, with benefits including pension, lunch, health insurance and social events.

• 
A strong team spirit where we celebrate wins and enjoy time together across offices.

• 
Our annual Global Summit, where the whole company meets and connects.

Our recruitment process

• 
Send your application and upload relevant information

• 
15–30-minute online interview with our Talent Acquisition team

• 
30-minute interview with our Hiring Manager

• 
30-minute interview with our interim Head of Talent Acquisition

• 
Completion of Personality Assessment

• 
In-person team workshop in Aarhus with representatives of People Operations, Workplace and Internal IT, where you work on a real case such as our future onboarding

About Formalize

Formalize is a tech company founded in 2021 with offices in Aarhus, Copenhagen, Milan, Munich and Madrid. Currently, we are a team of +200 people from +30 nationalities operating in multiple European markets and are one of the fastest growing SaaS scale-ups. We thrive on ambition, deliver impact through pragmatism, and embrace passion and honesty. We are celebrating our wins, learning from our mistakes, and growing together as a team.

Our journey began within the whistleblowing compliance sector, highlighted by the award-winning Whistleblower Software by Formalize, laying the foundation of our success story. Now, we have extended our expertise to a larger compliance universe, including data compliance, risk, and privacy. Our Formalize product helps companies to effortlessly navigate and stay ahead in the ever-changing landscape of compliance. Our platform adapts to regulatory changes, continuously adapting to meet and foresee the evolving needs of our users, ensuring businesses remain compliant and confident in their operations.

Still curious? Read more about us here: About Formalize.

Ready to apply?

We will hold interviews and hire on an ongoing basis. For more information or questions, please contact the responsible recruiter in the Talent Acquisition team. Apply now with your resume and other relevant information through our Career Page. We look forward to seeing your application!

Digital Marketing & E-commerce Specialist – Help Us Scale LeanSails Across Europe

Would you like to help grow a digital business and bring a traditional industry into the future?

At LeanSails, we're on a mission to make buying new sails easier, more transparent, and more affordable for sailors. We've developed a digital sales platform where boat owners can configure their own sails, explore different options, and get instant pricing online.

Having established our business in Denmark, we're now taking the next exciting step: expanding into Sweden, Finland, and eventually the rest of Europe.

We're looking for a Digital Marketing & E-commerce Specialist who is excited about taking ownership of our digital marketing activities and helping us grow our business.

Your Role

You'll become a key part of a small company with big ambitions. You'll have the opportunity to work across the entire digital customer journey – from the first ad impression to the moment a customer orders their new sails.

Your role will combine hands-on digital marketing with contributing to our growth strategy as we enter new markets.

Your responsibilities will include:

• 
Digital Advertising: Planning, setting up, managing, and optimizing campaigns on Google Ads, Facebook, and Instagram.

• 
SEO & Organic Traffic: Improving our search engine visibility and developing relevant content to attract potential customers.

• 
E-commerce Optimization: Improving our webshop, customer journey, and conversion rates.

• 
Data & Analytics: Using Google Analytics and other tools to understand customer behavior and improve marketing performance.

• 
International Expansion: Planning and executing marketing activities as we launch in new European markets.

• 
Business Development: Contributing ideas and initiatives to improve our digital business model and drive growth.

You'll have plenty of opportunities to shape your own responsibilities, bring new ideas to the table, and influence how we achieve our goals.

Who Are You?

We imagine you have a relevant educational background in digital marketing, e-commerce, communication, or a related field.

You might be a recent graduate or have a few years of professional experience. What matters most to us is your motivation, curiosity, willingness to take responsibility, and ability to turn ideas into action.

Ideally, you:

• 
Have an interest in, and preferably some hands-on experience with, Google Ads, Meta Ads, and digital marketing.

• 
Understand e-commerce and how to attract visitors and convert them into customers.

• 
Have an analytical mindset and enjoy using data to make decisions.

• 
Are proactive, independent, and comfortable experimenting with new ideas.

• 
Enjoy working in a small company where ideas can quickly turn into action.

• 
Communicate confidently in both Danish and English.

You don't need to know anything about sailing! We'll teach you what you need to know about the industry. Your interest in digital business, marketing, and growth is far more important.

What We Offer

At LeanSails, you won't be managing just one small part of a large marketing department.

You'll join a small, entrepreneurial team where you can work across different areas of digital marketing and see the direct impact of your efforts on the company's development.

We offer:

• 
An exciting position with real responsibility and the opportunity to make a difference.

• 
Hands-on experience with international e-commerce and digital business growth.

• 
An informal working environment with short decision-making processes.

• 
Close collaboration with experienced professionals from the sailmaking industry and business development.

• 
Great opportunities to develop your skills as the company grows.

• 
A workplace in Helsingør, Denmark, with flexibility in your daily work.

Employment Type

We are looking for a permanent employee to join the LeanSails team. This position is therefore not open to freelancers, independent consultants, or marketing agencies.

We welcome applications from both recent graduates and experienced candidates. Our priority is finding the right person who wants to become part of our company and contribute to its long-term development.

About LeanSails

LeanSails is a Danish e-commerce company selling custom-made sails directly to boat owners through an innovative digital platform.

We combine years of experience in the sailmaking industry with a modern digital business model that makes buying new sails simpler, more transparent, and more accessible.

Our ambition is to establish LeanSails as a strong European brand in online sail sales.

Ready to Join Us?

We'd love to hear from you!

Tell us a little about yourself, your experience, and why you think joining LeanSails could be an exciting opportunity.

We value motivation, curiosity, initiative, and the ability to make things happen more than a long list of previous job titles.

We look forward to hearing from you!

For more information or questions please contact us at info@leansails.dk or phone number +4527208349

_Do you enjoy turning data into insights and forecasts that help a global business make better decisions? Are you motivated by working across markets and functions, balancing availability, inventory and commercial priorities?

_We are looking for a Specialist, POSM Demand Planning to join our Global Merchandising & Supply Chain organisation in Copenhagen. In this role, you will support our global demand planning for Point of Sale Materials (POSM), covering areas such as packaging, accessories, displays, sellable items and services.

**Your role

**As our Demand Planning Specialist, you will help develop accurate, reliable and insight-driven item-level forecasts aligned with our commercial, marketing and inventory objectives.

You will work closely with clusters and global teams, with particular focus on new launches and item transitions. Through strong analysis and collaboration, you will help us improve availability while managing inventory and reducing the risk of obsolescence.

**Your Key Responsibilities

****In this role, you will:

**

• Support and execute the global POSM demand planning process, ensuring forecasts are delivered according to agreed timelines and standards.

• Consolidate and validate forecasts across clusters, ensuring strong data quality and timely cross-functional input.

• Develop item-level forecasts across packaging, accessories, displays and sellable POSM.

• Maintain statistical baseline forecasts using demand history, market intelligence, marketing plans, sell-in signals and lifecycle changes.

• Monitor forecast accuracy and bias, identify key demand drivers and conduct root-cause analyses to recommend corrective actions.

• Translate planning and performance data into clear, actionable insights and recommendations.

• Partner with Marketing, Clusters, Supply Planning and Procurement to build reliable forecasts for new launches and SKU transitions.

• Support phase-in and phase-out planning and proactively identify potential excess inventory, shortages and obsolescence risks.

• Work closely with clusters and global functions to align demand plans with commercial calendars, marketing campaigns, inventory targets and supply constraints.

• Contribute to improvements in planning processes, data and systems, helping strengthen planning quality, efficiency and inventory outcomes.

**What We’re Looking For

**You are analytical and comfortable working with data, but equally confident turning numbers into a clear story for stakeholders. You enjoy collaborating across functions and markets, challenging assumptions constructively and taking ownership when something needs to move forward.

**We Imagine That You Bring

**

• 1–3 years of relevant experience within Demand Planning, Supply Planning and/or Merchandise Planning.

• A relevant educational background in areas such as Supply Chain, Logistics, Engineering, Finance & Economics or International Business, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.

• Practical experience with forecasting, statistical modelling and root-cause analysis.

• An understanding of end-to-end supply chain and inventory trade-offs.

• Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills.

• The ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively across functions.

• A curious, proactive and solution-oriented mindset.

• Strong skills in Excel and PowerPoint.

• Experience with Logility or a similar demand planning system, and/or Aptos or another allocation system.

• Knowledge of Power BI, Power Query or QlikView is considered an advantage.

• Fluency in English.

Experience from retail, fashion or FMCG, as well as working in a global organisation across multiple markets or clusters, would be an advantage

**Additional Information

**

• Global Career Band 5B

**Did we get your attention?

**If you see yourself in the position and would like to become part of Pandora’s future, please do not hesitate to apply. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible.

You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site.

**About Pandora

**Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

With an IoT platform connecting more millions of devices, and growing - Trackunit is building the connectivity layer underneath the construction industry. Every one of those units carries a cellular radio, and every one of those radios sits inside a web of standards, type approvals, and patent licences that decides whether we can ship and where we can ship.

You will join our IoT Division, Device Reliability Engineering (DRE) team as an expert on IoT certifications, standards, and licensing including Standard Essential Patents (SEP). This position shapes both our exposure and our coverage arguments, and it means this role works in every direction at once, with suppliers, regulatory approvals, legal advisors, product and engineering, and with customers.

This is a role for someone who can hold a genuinely complex domain in their head and then explain it in three sentences to a customer who has never heard the phrase “patent exhaustion.”

Experience level: a deep specialist role. We expect solid, hands-on experience with cellular device approvals and licensing — likely 10+ years across regulatory, certification, or IP/licensing work in mobile, IoT, or telecom hardware. This is a senior individual contributor position with no direct reports, high autonomy, and direct executive visibility.

With locations in the heart of Copenhagen, Kolding, Aarhus, and Aalborg, we offer a flexible setup with the possibility to work from one of our locations — or remotely from anywhere in Denmark.

****What's in it for you?

• A domain you will own, not administer. IoT Cellular License, SEP and certification strategy is an executive-level topic at Trackunit right now, with real financial exposure attached. You will not be filing paperwork in a corner, you will be shaping the position the company takes.

• International environment with regular check-ins and social events across teams, departments and borders.

• We take your personal and professional development goals seriously and we support them through training, coaching, and mindfulness as well as with an open feedback culture to enable you to identify your strengths and opportunities.

• Flexibility and hybrid working is not just a cliché to us or something we state in a job posting. We offer a flexible setup because we believe you know best how to structure your work. Once you have chosen how you work best, let us know what you need: we got you covered with the IT equipment you need for your work.

• Turning the Tide. At Trackunit, we aim to create and contribute to an inclusive workplace. And this priority starts with our hiring — we do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity, sexual orientation, personal expression, ethnicity, religious belief, or disability status. We only assess candidates on their qualifications and merit. Learn more about TIDE and other DE&I initiatives here.

****What you'll do

****Your work splits roughly into four parts: licensing, approvals, guidance, and governance.

• Own our SEP position. Understand where our cellular SEP exposure actually sits across our device portfolio, track the relevant patent pools and licensing programmes, and maintain a clear, evidence-based view of what is covered through our supply chain and what is not.

• Run supplier licensing due diligence. Establish and maintain a consistent set of asks across module suppliers — coverage confirmation, standards and generations covered, and honest disclosure of known gaps — so responses can be compared side by side and fed into supplier qualification.

• Support licensing negotiations and claims. Work alongside our General Counsel, external patent counsel, and economic advisors on royalty basis questions, valuation and apportionment arguments, and claims that reach us through our OEM customers. You bring the technical and supply chain substance; they bring the legal strategy.

• Own global type approvals and certification. Plan and steer RED/CE, FCC, ISED, UKCA, and the wider set of regional approvals, plus GCF/PTCRB and carrier certification, across a multi-region device portfolio. Keep certification on the critical path of new product programmes rather than at the end of them.

• Stay ahead of regulatory change. Cyber Resilience Act, RED delegated acts, radio spectrum and network sunsets, environmental and product compliance requirements — know what is coming, when it bites, and what it means for our roadmap.

• Make the complex simple, and guide without over-promising. Write and maintain the internal playbooks, customer-facing explainers, and OEM guidance that turn this domain into something a commercial colleague or a customer can act on. Be the person Sales, Legal, and customers come to when a licensing notification lands, explaining the landscape accurately, saying clearly where the limits of our position are, and pointing customers to independent specialist advice where that is the right answer.

• Build the governance. Response protocols, decision records, escalation paths, and embedding licensing and compliance requirements into how we qualify suppliers and run the product development lifecycle.

****Who you are

****We think you'll need

• Strong working knowledge of cellular connectivity (e.g. LTE-M, NB-IoT, LTE Cat-1/1bis, 5G) and the direction of travel, plus a real understanding of the module and chipset landscape.

• Solid, practical experience with licensing and Standard Essential Patents in mobile or IoT devices: FRAND principles, patent pools, patent exhaustion and the limits of sublicensing, and how royalties are actually structured and argued.

• Hands-on experience with global type approvals and regulatory certification for radio products — RED/CE, FCC, and the regional approvals that come with selling hardware worldwide.

• Experience working across a hardware supply chain with module suppliers, test houses, notified bodies, and certification partners.

• Communication as a core skill, not a bonus. You can take a genuinely complicated subject and land it in plain language, in writing, with an audience that has no background in it.

• The judgement to know what we can and cannot say to a customer, and the discipline to hold that line even when it would be easier not to.

**What Matters More Than The Checklist

**

• You are honest about uncertainty. In this domain, no one can offer a blanket guarantee, and the people who claim otherwise create problems later. We would rather be accurate than reassuring.

• You are curious and self-driven, this is a field that changes constantly, and nobody is going to hand you a reading list.

• You finish things. A clear one-page answer delivered this week beats a perfect analysis that arrives after the decision was made.

• You are comfortable being the only person in the room who knows a subject, and you use that position to make others smarter rather than to make yourself indispensable.

On AI: experience with AI tooling is not a requirement, but a strong motivation and interest in working with it is. We already use AI in our daily engineering work, including MCP servers and agents against our own platform, and we see clear potential in applying it to research, documentation, and compliance workflows. We don't expect you to have experience with this but we do expect curiosity and a willingness to learn.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries this is what we're looking for ideally, but if you're excited about this role and your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification, we still encourage you to apply.

****How you'll grow here

****This is a specialist role with an unusually wide view of the business, and we've set it up that way on purpose.

• Executive proximity. You will work closely with the SVP of IoT Division, while reporting into a central function for IoT, as the Device Reliability Engineering. You will help in presenting to executive leadership on exposure, risk, and recommendations. Your analysis will inform on a product technical matter (Not Legal) but with real financial and commercial decisions.

• Cross-functional reach. Legal, Finance, Product Management, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Sales all depend on this domain. Few roles at Trackunit touch as many parts of the company.

• External network. You will work with external patent counsel, economic consultants, module suppliers, certification bodies, and industry forums — building a network that extends well beyond Trackunit.

• Room to define the function. This discipline is being built out now. What it becomes — and whether it grows into a team — is substantially yours to shape.

**Coming Together To Connect Construction

**We're committed to construction one of the largest industries in the world. Over the past two decades, Trackunit has been pioneering technological progress within construction. Today, we are not only a leading IoT provider but a thought leader, supporting and shaping the agenda for an entire industry on a global scale.

We believe in taking a people approach in everything we do. Being human-centric is not restricted to our products — it's a way of life at Trackunit. We're proud to be a truly global team. Our colleagues get together in hubs spread across the globe, but we embrace the idea of working remotely and in environments that inspire you. Everything we do, we do it to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry for the world.

Postdoc in Nutritional Metabolomics, Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports
 Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen

  Are you interested in metabolomics and its role in advancing nutrition research? Are you good at working independently, but also enjoy being part of an ambitious and collaborating team? Are you driven by challenging the status quo? Then you might be our new postdoc! The position is to be filled by 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  This 2-year postdoctoral position addresses latest innovations in biomarker-driven dietary assessment to improve nutrition research with a specific interest in cardiometabolic diseases. The primary tasks are to validate biomarkers for the intake of commonly consumed foods and to utilize them in estimating dietary intake in nutrition studies. For this, the postdoc will work with LC-MS metabolomics profiles of human samples and will develop data-driven frameworks for the implementation of biomarkers of food intake as dietary assessment tools. The position is affiliated with the Foodprints project funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation.

  Responsibilities and qualifications

  We are looking for a motivated postdoctoral researcher interested in elucidating how an objective dietary assessment contributes to a better understanding of diet-cardiometabolic risk interactions by performing metabolomics analyses and integrating omics with self-reported dietary data from human studies. Additionally, the candidate will be involved in the supervision of the group’s Ph.D., Master and Bachelor students. The work will involve:

   	
• LC-MS data extraction and preprocessing 	
• Integration of diet and metabolomics data through uni- and multivariate statistical analyses 	
• Collaboration with other researchers, technicians and students affiliated with the project 	
• Dissemination of results in the form of conference contributions and scientific publications 	
• Teaching at nutrition and metabolomics courses depending on interests/expertise   The candidate we seek

   	
• Has a PhD degree in metabolomics, chemometrics, bioinformatics or other related areas, ideally applied to human research 	
• Has demonstrated expertise in mass-spectrometric data analyses (e.g. metabolomics) 	
• Has demonstrated expertise in omics data integration and flair for programming (R is an advantage) 	
• Has an excellent publication track record (or equivalent experience) and strong scientific drive 	
• Is motivated by both personal and team accomplishments 	
• Thrives on multidisciplinary collaboration and is curious and open-minded 	
• Has experience and a proven track record of successful collaboration in diverse research environments   As a formal requirement, you must hold a PhD degree (or equivalent). Experience with nutrition research (dietary interventions and/or cohort studies) is an advantage.

  We offer

  The period of employment is 2 years. The expected starting date is 1st of April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  You will contribute to the activities of the Nutrition and Biomarkers Group led by Assistant Professor Catalina Cuparencu, which is embeded within the Nutrition, Microbiome and Metabolomics Research Group at Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports, Faculty of Science at University of Copenhagen. We offer a dynamic, sociable, collaborative, and international environment with exciting scientific challenges and opportunities to further develop your scientific career. Beyond our expertise in nutrition, microbiome and metabolomics, we offer access to our metabolomics facility and facilities dedicated to cohort- and intervention studies.

  The University is situated in Copenhagen, which is consistently rated among the world's top 10 most livable and sustainable cities. Life for families is made easier via a publicly supported daycare and healthcare system, dual-career opportunities, maternity/parental leave, and six weeks of annual vacation. International candidates may find useful information on living and working in Denmark. Useful information is also available at the university’s International Staff Mobility (ISM) office, which offers a variety of services to international researchers coming to and working at the University of Copenhagen.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include 

   	
• Application (Cover letter) 	
• CV 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent) 	
• Complete publication list   
 The deadline for applications is December 13, 2026, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. 

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews are expected to be held in January 2027.  

  Further information

  Further information about the position may be obtained from Assistant Professor Catalina Cuparencu, Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports, University of Copenhagen (cup@nexs.ku.dk)

  You can read more about the research group at
 https://nexs.ku.dk/english/research/nutrition-health/nutrition-microbiome-and-metabolomics/

  You can also read more about Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports, University of Copenhagen at www.nexs.ku.dk/english/

- for the developer who wants to build real things with AI

You write clean code, you have started integrating LLMs into real projects, and you are curious about what comes next. In Egmont's Data & AI Solutions team, you will build practical AI solutions - APIs, LLM wrappers, MCP connectors - that business teams across the Nordics depend on, while sharing ownership of the production systems that keep everything running. Hands-on from day one, with room to grow.

The role

You will be joining a team that builds and maintains AI and data solutions for business units across the Egmont Group - tools and integrations that people actually use.

Your work will cover three areas:

Build applied AI solutions. On top of Egmont’s AI platform infrastructure, you will build LLM wrappers, APIs, and MCP connectors - and take prototypes from concept to working solutions for business units with AI-related challenges.

Support Egmont's companies. You will work directly with companies across the Egmont Group, as both a hands-on builder and an advisor. That means helping business teams see where AI can make a real difference, shaping the right approach with them, and staying involved until it works in practice.

Keep things running - and make them better. You will share ownership of our Prefect-orchestrated Python pipelines alongside our senior engineers, handling operational triage, debugging, and continuous stability improvements.

What you bring

We care more about what you have built and how you think than about your job titles. That said, to hit the ground running, you will bring at least two years of experience in software development or a similar field, along with most of the following:

- Solid Python development experience - clean, modular code and confidence building and consuming APIs, including authentication, JSON and error handling

- Practical LLM integration experience - you have worked with language models in real settings and know your way around context engineering, MCP and agentic integrations

- An analytical and operational mindset - you keep the bigger picture in view, spot problems before they become incidents and take pride in systems that stay stable

Bonus points for experience with orchestration tools, lightweight frontends or Azure and AWS basics.

Beyond the technical, we are looking for someone curious and clear in their communication, who enjoys making technology accessible to non-technical colleagues. Knowledge of a Scandinavian language is an advantage, as Egmont is primarily a Nordic media group.

The team

You will be joining Data & AI Solutions - a tight-knit team of developers. We work closely with the platform team that runs the data and AI infrastructure our solutions are built on, so you will always have strong technical peers to spar with.

The role is based at Egmont's corporate office in Copenhagen. A flexible hybrid setup is possible, and we can agree on the balance between office and home days together.

And yes - the canteen is excellent.

Logistics & How to Apply

- Location: Copenhagen (hybrid possible)

- Application deadline: December 6, 2026

- Employment type: Full-time, permanent

To apply, please use the "Apply Now" button on this page. Note that we do not accept applications via email. Applications are welcome in Danish, Norwegian, Swedish or English.

We review applications continuously, so please apply as soon as possible.

If you have questions about the role, you are welcome to reach out to Hampus Vitestam, Manager Data & AI Solutions at hampus.vitestam@egmont.com.

About Egmont

Egmont is a leading Nordic media group focused on strong content and platforms within film, tv, cinema, streaming, gaming, e-commerce, marketing services, educational platforms, magazines and books. Proud owner of strong companies like Nordisk Film, TV 2 in Norway, Lindhardt og Ringhof and Story House Egmont. jobs.description:
Are you an experienced software engineer looking for something different? Imagine developing software in the morning, testing it on real hardware in the afternoon, and eventually watching it take flight.

At Acodyne, you will work alongside engineers developing next-generation unmanned aircraft, applying your software engineering experience to challenges that extend far beyond the screen.

You will have the opportunity to work across the software stack, from embedded systems and flight control integration to simulation, telemetry, and ground-based applications. You'll join a small, ambitious team where your contributions will have a direct impact on the aircraft we build.

Your Role

As part of our growing engineering team, you will develop and integrate software for our high-speed, heavy-lift cargo UAVs and their supporting systems.

You will work closely with electronics, mechanical, and aerospace engineers to turn ideas into working solutions, taking software from development through simulation, hardware integration, and real-world flight testing.

We believe that reliable software starts with good engineering practices. Code reviews, automated testing, continuous integration, and reproducible builds are important parts of how we want to develop our systems.

You will:

• 
Develop and maintain software for our aircraft and supporting systems.

• 
Work with embedded Linux platforms, flight computers, sensors, actuators, and communication systems.

• 
Integrate and extend existing flight control technologies such as ArduPilot or PX4.

• 
Develop tools for telemetry collection, monitoring, data analysis, and ground control.

• 
Build and maintain simulation environments and automated tests to validate software before flight.

• 
Contribute to reliable development workflows, continuous integration, testing, and release processes.

• 
Collaborate across engineering disciplines to integrate and troubleshoot software and hardware.

• 
Participate in prototype development, system integration, and flight test activities.

• 
Document software designs, interfaces, and test results to support future certification and compliance.

About You

We're looking for an experienced software engineer who enjoys solving challenging technical problems and takes pride in building reliable, maintainable software.

You've worked in a professional software development environment and understand the value of good engineering practices. Version control, code reviews, automated testing, continuous integration, and reproducible builds are a natural part of how you work.

You're comfortable taking ownership, making pragmatic engineering decisions, and collaborating with people from different technical backgrounds. You enjoy learning new technologies and aren't afraid to venture beyond your existing expertise.

You don't need to be an aerospace expert. We value strong software engineering fundamentals, technical curiosity, and the ability to master new domains.

You likely have:

•

• Experience with cloud infrastructure and distributed systems.

You enjoy reverse-engineering systems you do not control, finding structure in messy real-world data, and turning one-off discoveries into reusable software. You are comfortable being the engineer in the room with customers and partners.

Working at Apylon means embarking on a highly ambitious mission to rebuild the financial infrastructure of European healthcare. PhD Project in Muscular signaling and metabolism

  Nutrition Exercise and Sports (NEXS), Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen

  The August Krogh Section for Human and Molecular Physiology at Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in “Elucidating the role of AMPK in Skeletal Muscular signaling and metabolism”. The project is part of the research project “Illuminating the signaling architecture of skeletal muscle insulin resistance”, which is financed by the Novo Nordisk Foundation

  Start date is (expected to be) 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project

  By the use of phophosproteomics in human skeletal muscle, we recently discovered a novel phosphorylation site on AMPK alpha2 subunit regulated by mTORC1. This phosphorylation is associate with glucose uptake. We now wish to explore the relationship between the catabolic signal from AMPK and the anabolic signal from mTORC1 and the potential causal link to metabolic regulation. The project will primarily be conducted in mice by the use of transgenic KI models.

  Who are we looking for?

  We welcome applications from candidates with a strong academic background in physiology, biology, biomedical sciences, exercise science or a related field, and an interest in skeletal muscle physiology and metabolic regulation.

  The project combines animal studies with molecular and metabolic analyses. Experience in one or more relevant areas is an advantage, but applicants are not expected to have all of the skills already. Relevant experience could include in vivo or ex vivo research, metabolic phenotyping, muscle physiology, tissue processing, immunoblotting, immunoprecipitation or tracer-based assays.

  An interest in molecular signalling pathways involved in metabolism, including AMPK and nutrient sensing, would be valuable. Above all, we are looking for a curious and motivated researcher who is keen to learn and develop within a collaborative research environment.

  Our group and research- and what do we offer?

  The group is a part of Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports at the Faculty of Scince, University of Copenhagen. We are located in Copenhagen.

  We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and animal facilities.

  Our group work focuses on the molecular mechanisms through which physical activity promotes metabolic health.

  We are particularly interested in the intracellular interactions between exercise-induced signaling events and those triggered by insulin, aiming to unravel how a single bout of exercise can enhance muscle insulin sensitivity. Central to these studies is the role of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and its interacting partners, including mTOR and TBC1D4.

  We are studying this in humans using various cell/animal models for validation and mechanistic analyses.

  Principal supervisor is Professor Jørgen Wojtaszewski (NEXS, JW@nexs.ku.dk, 45 28751625) and Associate professor Rasmus Kjøbsted (NEXS, Rasmus.Kjobsted@nexs.ku.dk, 45 28344370)

Postdoctoral Researcher in Human Skin Biology and Wound Healing

  Department of Biology, Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen

  The Department of Biology at the University of Copenhagen invites applications for a postdoctoral researcher in human skin biology and wound healing. The position is part of a newly established research group investigating how cells coordinate their behaviour to maintain and repair tissues.

  The position is fully funded for at least 2 years, with the possibility of extension, through generous funding from the LEO Foundation. The earliest possible start date is 1 April 2027. Please clearly state your availability and preferred start date in your cover letter.

  Information about the Department of Biology is available at https://www1.bio.ku.dk/english/. Information about the specific research section you will be affiliated with is available at https://www1.bio.ku.dk/english/research/cbp/.

  Project overview

  The overarching aim is to develop strategies to help people with slow- or non-healing wounds.

  This project investigates how planar cell polarity (PCP)—the coordinated orientation of cells within a tissue—contributes to human skin organization and wound repair. Although PCP signaling is essential for tissue organization across many organisms, its role in human epidermis remains poorly understood.

  You will establish reconstructed human epidermis (RHE) as an experimental model to investigate PCP signaling in human skin, then use advanced fluorescence microscopy to characterize PCP clusters, their polarization, and how they change during wound repair and in response to other stressors.

  The project bridges fundamental questions in cell and developmental biology with potential long-term applications in regenerative medicine and skin repair. It is supported by collaborators with expertise in RHE development and by access to confocal and advanced microscopy, including SIM, TIRF, and STED.

  The project provides a clear starting point and room to shape the research questions as findings emerge. In your cover letter, please clearly describe what interests you about the project and what related research questions you would be excited to explore.

  We are seeking a motivated, technically skilled, and scientifically independent postdoctoral researcher to play a central role in establishing this research programme. As one of the first members of a newly established research group, you will have an exceptional opportunity to shape its experimental approaches, contribute to its scientific direction, and help build a collaborative, ambitious research environment.

In the cover letter, you are encouraged to highlight an example of experimental independence, including situations in which you have established or substantially improved an experimental method, solved a challenging technical problem, or independently advanced a research project.

• Experience with confocal microscopy or an advanced imaging technique such as SIM, TIRF, or STED.

Dalux continues to grow rapidly, and AI is creating entirely new possibilities for how construction professionals find information, understand complex project data, automate repetitive work, and make decisions.

We're looking for an AI Product Manager to help turn those possibilities into products that create real value for our users.

As an AI Product Manager at Dalux, you'll operate at the intersection of customer needs, rapidly evolving AI technology, and business strategy. You'll work closely with Product Design, AI engineers, developers, and other Product Managers to identify where AI can meaningfully improve construction workflows – and equally importantly, where it cannot.

Building AI products is different from traditional software development. Outputs are probabilistic, quality needs continuous evaluation, and product decisions involve trade-offs between accuracy, latency, cost, scalability, and user trust.

You'll help us navigate those trade-offs and establish how we build great AI products at Dalux.

**Your responsibilities will include:

**

• AI Product Discovery: Identify and validate problems where AI can create meaningful value rather than applying AI for its own sake.

• Customer Insights: Work closely with users and internal domain experts to understand construction workflows and identify opportunities for AI-powered improvements.

• Evaluation & Quality: Define what "good" looks like for AI features and establish evals, quality metrics, test cases, and feedback loops.

• AI Safety & Trust: Consider hallucinations, uncertainty, guardrails, failure modes, explainability, and user trust throughout product development.

• Feature Ownership: Lead AI-powered features from early experimentation and prototyping through delivery, evaluation, and continuous improvement.

• Technical Collaboration: Work closely with AI engineers and developers on model capabilities, context, architecture, latency, scalability, and cost.

• AI Product Strategy: Follow developments in models and AI technology and help determine which technological advances create meaningful opportunities for Dalux.

**About You

**We are looking for someone who combines strong product thinking with a solid understanding of modern AI.

You don't need to be an AI engineer, but you need enough technical understanding to make informed product decisions and have meaningful discussions with the engineers building these systems.

We believe you:

• Have experience building or managing customer-facing AI/ML products.

• Understand concepts such as LLMs, RAG, embeddings, context, agents, evals, and guardrails.

• Understand the fundamental difference between building deterministic software and probabilistic AI experiences.

• Can translate rapidly evolving technical capabilities into valuable user experiences.

• Are comfortable defining and measuring quality where traditional acceptance criteria are insufficient.

• Think critically about when AI is – and isn't – the right solution.

• Can balance user value, model quality, latency, scalability, and cost.

• Communicate fluently in English, written and spoken.

Experience with B2B SaaS is an advantage.

Experience with construction technology is welcome but not required. We have deep construction expertise within Dalux – for this role, we are particularly interested in adding strong AI product expertise to our organization.

We offer:

• A collaborative and informal work environment with flat hierarchies

• High ownership, trust, and the freedom to drive initiatives

• Talented and dedicated colleagues in an international team

• A central Copenhagen office, flexible work hours, and no dress code

• Monthly social events and an active community

• Attractive benefits including health insurance, lunch, fitness facilities, and free parking

About Sparrow Quantum

Sparrow Quantum is a Danish quantum technology company advancing light-matter interfaces for quantum technologies and is widely recognized as a leader in single-photon sources.

Our first product is an on-chip single-photon source that delivers more than 20 million high-quality single photons per second into an optical fiber, used by customers for applications such as multi-photon quantum simulation and quantum key distribution.

The patented technology builds on more than two decades of research by founder Peter Lodahl and the Hy-Q Center of Excellence at the Niels Bohr Institute in Copenhagen. Learn more at www.sparrowquantum.com.
